Context only. Conditions 2 and 3 distinguish altered-source marking from source-notice preservation. The FAQ supplies the package classification.

challenge.method: Compared four cases: compiled library alone, library plus one header, library plus both headers with alterations, and that same combination without alterations. Checked the FAQ’s classification and marking instruction separately.
challenge.results: The FAQ expressly classifies the library-plus-both-headers combination, even though it includes compiled code. It directs version and change marking for alterations. It gives no direction to label unchanged source as altered. Its example does not classify the binary-only or one-header cases. Source-notice preservation is a separate condition whenever a covered source distribution is made.

limitations: The documented classification covers the named three-part combination. Binary-only, one-header and other package configurations require separate evidence. No actual shipment was examined.
reasoning: FAQ 24 expressly classifies distribution of a compiled zlib library together with zlib.h and zconf.h as a source distribution. In its discussion of alterations, the publisher directs the distributor to change both version definitions and record the origin and nature of the changes in zlib.h.
